title: TB preventive treatment (NTEP)
subject: infectious-disease
setting: Outpatient, TB unit, ART centre, primary care
summary: Rule out active TB (symptoms, chest X-ray, NAAT if symptomatic), then give TPT to people with HIV, all household contacts of pulmonary TB (testing for infection when available but never a barrier) and tested high-risk groups, using 3HP or 6H (or 1HP, 3RH), with 6Lfx or 4R for contacts of drug-resistant TB.

sections.title: Who should receive TPT (NTEP PMTPT 2021)
items: People living with HIV, adults and children over 12 months: TPT for all once active TB is excluded, irrespective of CD4 count, ART status, previous TB treatment or pregnancy. Infants under 12 months with HIV: TPT (6H) only if they are contacts of a TB patient and active TB is excluded.

Household contacts of pulmonary TB (bacteriologically confirmed index patients prioritised): under 5 years, TPT after ruling out TB without any infection test; 5 years and older, TPT if TST, IGRA or Cy-Tb is positive or unavailable and chest X-ray is normal or unavailable.

Other risk groups (immunosuppressive or anti-TNF therapy, silicosis, dialysis, preparing for organ or haematological transplant): test for TB infection first and give TPT only if positive with a normal chest X-ray.
Contacts of MDR/RR-TB with a fluoroquinolone-sensitive index: 6Lfx. Contacts of isoniazid-resistant, rifampicin-sensitive TB: 4R. NTEP (August 2025) directs all states to offer these.
Diabetes, undernutrition, smoking or alcohol use alone are not indications for systematic testing and TPT.

sections.title: Rule out active TB first
items: Symptom screen: people with HIV use the 4-symptom screen (current cough, fever, weight loss, night sweats). Others: any cough, fever, night sweats, haemoptysis, weight loss, chest pain, breathlessness or fatigue; in children under 5 also poor appetite, failure to thrive or reduced playfulness.
Any symptom or an abnormal chest X-ray: investigate for TB (sputum NAAT) and treat if confirmed; do not start TPT.
Chest X-ray wherever available; lack of an X-ray or infection test must not delay TPT for people with HIV or child contacts.
Contacts of DR-TB: symptom assessment and chest X-ray, with upfront NAAT, before choosing 6Lfx or 4R according to the index patient's resistance pattern.

Contraindications: active TB, acute or chronic hepatitis, other hepatotoxic drugs (e.g. nevirapine), regular heavy alcohol use, peripheral neuropathy (for isoniazid), hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and previous TB are not contraindications.

sections.title: Regimens for contacts of drug-susceptible TB and other groups
items: 3HP: weekly isoniazid plus rifapentine for 12 doses (age over 2 years). Preferred for its short course; give each dose supervised.
6H: daily isoniazid for 6 months (182 doses). Use in pregnancy, infants and whenever rifapentine is unsuitable.
1HP (NTEP addendum 2024): daily isoniazid 300 mg plus rifapentine 600 mg for 28 doses, age 13 years and older.
3RH (NTEP addendum 2024): daily rifampicin plus isoniazid for 3 months (84 doses) in children under 15 years.

Rifapentine regimens are contraindicated with protease inhibitors, nevirapine and other NNRTIs, and tenofovir alafenamide; they can be used with tenofovir disoproxil, efavirenz 600 mg, dolutegravir and raltegravir without dose change. Rifamycins lower hormonal contraceptive levels.

Pyridoxine with isoniazid-containing regimens for those at risk of neuropathy (undernutrition, alcohol dependence, HIV, renal failure, diabetes, pregnancy, breastfeeding). Do not withhold TPT if pyridoxine is unavailable.

sections.title: Regimens for contacts of drug-resistant TB
items: 6Lfx: daily levofloxacin for 6 months for contacts of rifampicin-resistant, fluoroquinolone-sensitive TB. Watch children for joint problems; levofloxacin 100 mg dispersible tablets are available.
4R: daily rifampicin for 4 months for contacts of isoniazid-resistant, rifampicin-sensitive TB (in children 0 to 14 years only in designated areas for evidence generation).
Contacts of RR-TB whose index isolate is sensitive to both fluoroquinolones and isoniazid: 6H can be used.
Manage adverse reactions and refer any contact with symptoms to the DR-TB centre for NAAT and LPA.

sections.title: Monitoring, interruptions and follow-up
items: Review monthly (or at every contact): adherence, TB symptoms, adverse effects (hepatitis, rash, neuropathy, flu-like illness with 3HP), interacting drugs. Stop and seek review for jaundice, dark urine, abdominal pain or vomiting.
Baseline LFT is not mandatory but is encouraged in liver disease, regular alcohol use, HIV, pregnancy or within 3 months postpartum; repeat as clinically indicated.

Missed doses (6H, 6Lfx, 4R): under 2 weeks, resume and extend by the missed days. Over 2 weeks: complete if more than 80% of doses were taken or the course can finish within 133% of the planned time; otherwise restart.

3HP: up to 3 missed weekly doses, continue until 12 doses (maximum 16 weeks), keeping doses at least 4 days apart; 4 or more missed, restart or switch to a daily regimen. Stop 3HP if pregnancy is detected and switch to 6H.
After completing TPT, follow up at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months for signs of active TB; record all TPT in Ni-kshay (contact and other risk group register).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Giving isoniazid alone to someone with undiagnosed active TB, which breeds resistance: always screen symptoms and do an X-ray or NAAT when indicated.
Deferring TPT for child contacts or people with HIV because TST, IGRA or X-ray is unavailable.
Starting rifapentine or rifampicin with protease inhibitors or nevirapine, or without advising on contraceptive failure.
Using 6H or 3HP for contacts of MDR-TB, or ignoring the index patient's drug-resistance pattern.

drugs.name: Isoniazid (6H)
drugs.dose: Age 10 years and older: 5 mg/kg orally once daily (maximum 300 mg). Under 10 years: 10 mg/kg once daily (range 7 to 15 mg/kg, maximum 300 mg). For 6 months
drugs.notes: Safe in pregnancy. Add pyridoxine if at risk of neuropathy.

drugs.name: 3HP: isoniazid plus rifapentine weekly
drugs.dose: Over 14 years (30 kg and more): isoniazid 900 mg (3 x 300 mg) plus rifapentine 900 mg (6 x 150 mg), or 3 tablets of HP FDC 300/300 mg, once weekly for 12 weeks. Age 2 to 14 years weekly: 10 to 15 kg H 300 mg + P 300 mg; 16 to 23 kg H 500 mg + P 450 mg; 24 to 30 kg H 600 mg + P 600 mg; 31 kg and above H 700 mg + P 750 mg
drugs.notes: Supervised doses; flu-like and hypersensitivity reactions; not known safe in pregnancy.

drugs.name: 1HP: isoniazid plus rifapentine daily
drugs.dose: Age 13 years and older: isoniazid 300 mg plus rifapentine 600 mg orally once daily for 28 days

drugs.name: 3RH: rifampicin plus isoniazid daily
drugs.dose: Under 15 years for 3 months: rifampicin 15 mg/kg (range 10 to 20) and isoniazid 10 mg/kg (range 7 to 15) daily if under 10 years; 10 mg/kg and 5 mg/kg if 10 years or older. RH 75/50 mg dispersible FDC: 4 to 7 kg 1 tablet; 8 to 11 kg 2; 12 to 15 kg 3; 16 to 24 kg 4; 25 kg and above adult formulation

drugs.name: Rifampicin (4R)
drugs.dose: Age 10 years and older: 10 mg/kg orally once daily (maximum 600 mg). Under 10 years: 15 mg/kg once daily (range 10 to 20 mg/kg, maximum 600 mg). For 4 months

drugs.name: Levofloxacin (6Lfx)
drugs.dose: Over 14 years: below 45 kg 750 mg once daily; 45 kg and above 1 g once daily. Under 15 years (about 15 to 20 mg/kg/day): 5 to 9 kg 150 mg; 10 to 15 kg 200 to 300 mg; 16 to 23 kg 300 to 400 mg; 24 to 34 kg 500 to 750 mg once daily. For 6 months
drugs.notes: Contacts of MDR/RR-TB with fluoroquinolone-sensitive index. Watch for tendon and joint problems.

drugs.name: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6)
drugs.dose: Children 10 mg, adults 25 mg, adults with HIV 50 mg orally once daily during isoniazid-containing TPT
drugs.notes: Treat established neuropathy with higher doses and stop isoniazid.
